evidence.title: Rookery Fleet lifecycle
evidence.finding: Persistent worker IDs/worktrees/branches; lazy SDK resume after daemon restart if session/worktree exist, otherwise orphaned. Stop keeps branch; discard destroys. Checkpoint restores only non-running work. GitOps does not commit/push/openPR; worker bash does when instructed.

evidence.title: Rookery Master and worker turns
evidence.finding: Master turns serialized, workers have FIFO pending followups. Worker completion notifies parent, persisted pending notification retry. Per-turn trusted capability overlays and separate generated Codex homes; live reload explicitly required for worker.

evidence.title: Rookery Automation architecture
evidence.finding: Persisted cron/once and Slack triggers route to master or worker; cron overlap skipped, Slack concurrent, once rearmed after crash for at-least-once. Older doc omits newer budget/trigger work, checked against pinned source.

evidence.title: Rookery Settings
evidence.finding: Settings stored locally, secret getters write-only; binds127.0.0.1 default, warns for plaintext token on remote bind. Slack allowlist fail-closed; API-key fallback to native CLI OAuth.

evidence.title: Rookery worker budget and recovery

evidence.finding: Worker checks per-send turn count, lifetime USD budget and repeated aborted/errored turns. Codex reports one subturn so maxTurns>1 does not cap Codex; cost budget is its runaway guard. Stops at observed result boundary, not hard prepaid guarantee.

evidence.title: Rookery fleet implementation

evidence.title: Rookery: docs/architecture/overview.md
evidence.locator: System shape; apps/desktop Electron main/preload; daemon HTTP route and origin checks
evidence.finding: The complete thin-client inventory is native Electron desktop, CLI and embedded Slack. The daemon serves health/control/MCP and WebSocket commands; it does not serve a standalone browser frontend. The renderer depends on an Electron preload bridge and the development Vite server is not a released browser product. No native iOS/Android client is supplied; Slack mobile is a third-party client.

evidence.title: Rookery: src/daemon/server.ts
evidence.locator: workerBackends and SessionManager backends composition; README Backends & authentication
evidence.finding: The product-owned session and worker backend registries contain only Claude and Codex. External MCP can be called by Cursor or other clients to drive Rookery workers, but it does not launch those client harnesses as Rookery agents. The registry has no user custom-agent adapter path.

evidence.title: Rookery: docs/reference/settings-and-env.md
evidence.locator: ROOKERY_HOST; README Headless / CLI; src/daemon/server.ts remote bind gate
evidence.finding: The documented headless daemon can bind an operator-selected network host through ROOKERY_HOST with an explicit ROOKERY_ALLOW_NONLOOPBACK override. CLI, external MCP and Slack act as clients of its resident process; daemon sessions/workers survive client disconnects. An operator can deploy that headless daemon on their server; no Rookery-managed compute service is implemented.

evidence.title: Rookery: src/core/fleet-orchestrator.ts
evidence.locator: Worker spawn/rehydration; src/core/git-ops.ts; Claude/Codex backend process launch
evidence.finding: Workers run native provider processes rooted in product-managed Git worktrees on the daemon host. The bounded spawn/backend paths implement no Docker/container or VM provisioning; a logical container session in session-manager.ts is a database/session grouping, not OS isolation.

evidence.title: Rookery: src/slack/handle-incoming.ts
evidence.finding: Slack input independently checks each human user ID against the allowlist (or configured allow-all). Session identity is team/channel/thread, not sender ID, so distinct permitted Slack users in the same thread call the same master session. The prompt prefix retains each sender name/ID. This uses separate human Slack identities, not a shared owner token.

evidence.title: Rookery: src/persistence/db.ts
evidence.locator: Complete schema/migrations; repositories.ts; docs/reference/data-model.md and protocol/messages.ts
evidence.finding: The complete persisted/domain model contains conversations, worker agent sessions, worktrees/checkpoints, memories, repos, automations and capability settings. Worker ticket_key/ticket_url are external ticket references. There is no independent native issue/task record or lifecycle distinct from these agent sessions; provider workflow-task events remain harness session activity.

evidence.title: Rookery: src/daemon/auth.ts
evidence.locator: Daemon token/origin authorization; Slack user allowlist; settings schema; external MCP scopes
evidence.finding: The daemon uses a local/shared capability token and Slack checks allowed human IDs. External MCP offers read-only versus full-control tool scope, without a named human membership/role permission matrix. The bounded source contains no enterprise SAML/OIDC SSO path; Slack/provider authentication is separate.

evidence.title: Rookery: src/core/settings.ts
evidence.locator: Settings and env registry; result-telemetry.ts; README Data handling
evidence.finding: The complete source settings/CLI contain no ADE analytics opt-out switch. result-telemetry.ts computes provider token/context usage for the local interface, and README says history, memory, tokens and logs stay local while task context goes to the chosen model provider. No ADE analytics reporter is present in the inspected runtime; provider telemetry controls are separate.
